questions.say: Good morning. My name is Emma, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about your hometown. Where did you grow up?

questions.text: Describe a film that you watched recently.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a film that you watched recently. You should say: what the film was; where and when you watched it; what happened in it; and explain what you thought of it.

questions.text: Would you watch this film again?
questions.say: Thank you. Would you watch this film again?

questions.text: Why do people still go to the cinema when they can watch films at home?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a film you watched recently, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all cinema and entertainment. Why do people still go to the cinema when they can watch films at home?

questions.text: Do films from other countries help people understand different cultures?
questions.say: Do films from other countries help people understand different cultures?

questions.text: Should there be age limits on the films children can watch?
questions.say: Now let's talk about films and young people. Should there be age limits on the films children can watch?

questions.text: Can films be a good way to learn about history?

questions.text: Do actors have too much influence on young people?
